content.user_title: Build Azure File Share Workflows in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure File Share integrations require correct authentication, client hierarchy, and transfer methods. This skill provides focused TypeScript guidance for shares, directories, files, snapshots, and SAS workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation and four Azure File Share authentication approaches.
Explains how to create, list, inspect, resize, and delete shares.
Covers directory creation, listing, existence checks, and deletion.
Demonstrates file uploads and downloads using strings, buffers, streams, and local paths.
Covers copy, metadata, HTTP headers, ranges, snapshots, SAS tokens, and error handling.
Identifies SDK features that differ between Node.js and browser environments.
limitations: Provides reference guidance only and includes no executable scripts.
Requires an Azure Storage account, suitable permissions, credentials, and network access.
Uses placeholder names and paths that require environment-specific validation.
Several authentication and file transfer methods work only in Node.js.

use_cases.title: Create a file service integration
use_cases.description: Select authentication and client patterns for a new TypeScript service that manages Azure file shares.

use_cases.title: Automate large file transfers
use_cases.description: Choose streaming, local file, buffer, or range methods for reliable uploads and downloads.

use_cases.title: Review storage implementation choices
use_cases.description: Compare permissions, SAS lifetimes, snapshots, quotas, and platform support before approving an integration.

prompt_templates.title: Set up an Azure File client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install the Azure File Share SDK and create a TypeScript client with DefaultAzureCredential. Use an environment variable for the account name.

prompt_templates.title: Manage shares and directories
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript workflow that creates a share with a quota, creates nested directories, and lists their contents. Include idempotent existence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer a large local file
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Node.js upload approach for a large local file. Explain stream settings, destination creation, error handling, and safe path validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design secure delegated access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a read-only file access flow using a short-lived SAS token. Cover permission scope, expiration, secret handling, logging, and snapshot recovery.

output_examples.input: Create a production authentication plan for an Azure-hosted TypeScript service.
output: Recommended authentication: managed identity through DefaultAzureCredential.
Required setting: the Azure Storage account name.
Validation: confirm File service data permissions before testing share access.

output_examples.input: Choose an upload method for a 500 MB local file.
output: Use a Node.js file stream and the SDK streaming upload method.
Validate the local path and file size before opening the stream.
Tune buffer size and concurrency under realistic network conditions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe document replacement workflow.
output: Create a share snapshot before changing the document.
Upload the replacement with explicit content settings and error handling.
Keep snapshot deletion separate from the replacement operation.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity and DefaultAzureCredential for production workloads.
Use short-lived, least-privilege SAS tokens and keep them out of logs.
Validate local paths, quotas, transfer sizes, and Azure permissions before operations.
anti_patterns: Do not embed account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens in source code.
Do not use browser environments for SDK methods marked as Node.js only.
Do not delete shares or snapshots without confirming scope and recovery requirements.

faq.question: Which Azure package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers @azure/storage-file-share for JavaScript and TypeScript, with @azure/identity for token-based authentication.

faq.question: Does it support managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance uses DefaultAzureCredential, which can use managed identity in a configured Azure environment.

faq.question: Can I use every example in a browser?
faq.answer: No. Shared key credentials, local file methods, streaming methods, buffer downloads, and SAS generation are Node.js-only.

faq.question: Does the skill execute Azure operations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference patterns that must be adapted, reviewed, and run in your own project.

faq.question: How should I transfer large files?
faq.answer: Use streaming uploads or direct file downloads in Node.js. Test buffer size and concurrency for your workload.

faq.question: How should credentials be protected?
faq.answer: Prefer managed identity. Otherwise, store secrets outside source control, limit permissions, rotate credentials, and never log SAS URLs.
